name: Enggano Thrush
rangeDescription: Enggano island (off southwestern sumatra)
description: Small, ornate thrush found only on Enggano, off the coast of Sumatra. Inhabits native forest and forest edge, where it tends to forage on the ground in areas with a well-shaded understory.

name: Jerdon's Courser
rangeDescription: Tropical scrub jungle of eastern ghats of andhra pradesh (east-central india); extremely rare, with no recent records
description: A delicate lapwing-like bird with a large eye and a short, bicolored bill. Note the strong white eyebrow and the brown breast with two distinct white bands.

name: Chilean Pigeon
rangeDescription: Araucaria and nothofagus forest and adjacent fields of central and southern chile and adjacent argentina
description: Only large native pigeon in its range. Locally fairly common in temperate rainforest, farmland with wooded patches, and matorral with taller trees.

name: White-headed Robin-Chat
rangeDescription: Savanna and forest of northwestern angola and adjacent western democratic republic of the congo
description: A beautiful and distinctive robin-chat with a white head, orange underparts, and a brown back. The very long tail has a dark center and broad orange sides.

name: Capped Heron
rangeDescription: Lowlands of eastern panama to the guianas, brazil, and northern paraguay
description: This gorgeous medium-sized heron is uncommon but widespread in lowlands of South America, barely extending into eastern Panama. Not likely to be mistaken: combination of silvery back, buffy neck and belly, black cap, and blue lores (sometimes radiant turquoise!) help distinguish this species from other herons.

name: Smooth-billed Ani
rangeDescription: West indies, southeastern mexico (quintana roo) and costa rica southward to western ecuador and northern argentina, also galapagos (introduced); formerly southeastern usa (florida, where now rare)
description: Anis are bizarre, coal-black cuckoos with long floppy tails and unique, curiously tall, flattened bills. Smooth-billed occurs in a variety of open and semi-open habitats in tropical lowlands and foothills, typically staying low in shrubs and grasses.

name: Kai Kecil White-eye
rangeDescription: Kai kecil (kai islands)
description: A small green-and-yellow songbird, green above with a yellow rump and a uniform yellow underside. No noticeable eye-ring.

name: White-browed Ground-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Andes of central and southern chile and adjacent argentina; winters to southern ecuador
description: Common summer resident in the Andes of central Chile and adjacent Argentina; migrates north in winter. Found on rocky and stony slopes with scrubby bushes, gravel plains, bogs, and lakeshores; often the commonest ground-tyrant, associating readily with other species in migrant flocks.

name: Large-billed Reed Warbler
rangeDescription: Breeds southeastern kazakhstan, northeastern afghanistan; winters myanmar, thailand; long known only from one 1867 specimen from northern india, distribution still poorly known
description: Poorly known, small gray-brown bird with a large bill, a flat forehead, and a short, pale supercilium. Extremely similar to Blyth’s Reed Warbler, but the Large-billed Reed Warbler has a longer bill, longer legs, and slightly shorter wings.

name: White-spotted Wattle-eye
rangeDescription: Forest of southern ivory coast to nigeria, gabon, and northern democratic republic of the congo
description: A pied wattle-eye of lowland forests. Males are white below with an iridescent black belt.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Three-toed Jacamar
rangeDescription: Lowlands of southeastern brazil (minas gerais to paraná)
description: Its small head, very long, straight bill, and long tail give it a distinctive silhouette. Mostly dark brown above with a streaky crown and whitish belly.

name: Red-legged Cormorant
rangeDescription: Coastal peru and chile; isolated population in southern argentina
description: Attractive coastal cormorant; locally fairly common in Humboldt Current. Often seen perched on jetties, inshore rocks, and cliffs associating readily with Guanay Cormorant, pelicans, boobies, and Inca Terns.

name: Great Hornbill
rangeDescription: Lowlands of india to southwestern china, southeastern asia, and sumatra
description: A huge, distinctive hornbill with a large yellow bill and casque. Black face, wings, and breast contrast with white neck, belly, and tail.

name: Santa Marta Foliage-gleaner
rangeDescription: Santa marta mountains (northeastern colombia)
description: A shy, uniformly chestnut-brown bird found in the foothills and lower slopes of Colombia’s Santa Marta Mountains. It lacks strong field marks, but has a rather stout bill and is slightly paler on the chin and around the eye.

name: Fawn-breasted Wren
rangeDescription: Northern bolivia, adjacent southwestern brazil (southwestern mato grosso), and paraguay
description: A rather nondescript medium-sized wren. Mostly brown above and rusty below, with a white eyebrow and pied streaked cheeks.

name: Redhead
rangeDescription: Alaska to southern usa; winters to guatemala and greater antilles
description: This attractive diving duck often gathers by the thousands on lakes or bays in the winter. Males have cinnamon-colored head, yellow eye, and gray body.

name: Socotra Warbler
rangeDescription: Socotra (off eastern somalia)
description: Drab little warbler endemic to Socotra. Gray-brown above and pale gray below, sometimes showing a brighter rufous coloration crown.

name: Pemba Scops-Owl
rangeDescription: Pemba island (off northeastern tanzania)
description: A large scops-owl that is endemic to the Tanzanian island of Pemba. A fairly plain owl with small ear tufts.

name: Red-chested Cuckoo
rangeDescription: Intra-african migrant south of the sahara
description: A mostly grayish cuckoo with banding below, including a broad rusty band across the upper breast. The immature has barred underparts and a charcoal back, throat, and breast.

name: Bay-chested Warbling Finch
rangeDescription: Scrub of southeastern brazil (minas gerais to northern río grande do sul)
description: Small finch with a conspicuous chestnut breast and flanks. Gray above with a white throat and belly and a white arc below the eye.
